title: Mental Crisis Prediction
description: Built an ML model with NHS Birmingham predicting mental health crises four weeks in advance at 80% recall, giving clinicians enough lead time to intervene before patients reached crisis point.

metrics.label: accuracy predicting mental health crisis 4 weeks ahead

sections.title: Context
sections.body: VP of Product & Innovation at Koa Health (Series B), in collaboration with Birmingham and Solihull NHS Foundation Trust. 1.2M patients covered.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Mental health crises are costly and traumatic — for patients and the health system. An unplanned hospital admission for a mental health crisis costs multiples of planned care. Clinicians had no early warning signal: by the time deterioration was visible, it was often too late for low-cost intervention. The business need was to demonstrate clinical and commercial value to NHS partners to secure ongoing contracts and investment.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I led the product definition, data partnership structuring, and NHS relationship. I personally owned the information governance negotiation, the data sharing agreements, and the clinical validation process with NHS partners. I also led the design of the clinician-facing interface. Data science modelling was delegated to the technical team.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: The model used de-identified NHS Electronic Health Records (178 features, 1 million patients over 6 years, 20,000 mental health patients) as the primary training signal, combined with real-time environmental factors and passive mobile sensor data. The four-week prediction horizon was a deliberate clinical decision — long enough to enable a proactive response, short enough to be actionable. I worked with NHS clinicians to define the alert logic so that outputs were filtered to patients not already on an active crisis plan, avoiding alert fatigue.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
• Model achieved 75% accuracy (80% recall) predicting mental health crisis four weeks in advance
  • Clinicians could schedule reviews, adjust medication, or increase support before patients reached crisis point
  • The project contributed to the evidence base that helped Koa Health secure investment and NHS partnerships, including a subsequent contract with Janssen
